title: Release Security Acceptance Playbook and Exception Approval
content:
Purpose:
This playbook standardizes the security review, evidence collection, and exception approval flow for product releases that touch RBAC v2, audit logging, or SIEM integrations. It is intended for Security reviewers, Release Managers, Product Owners, SREs, and Engineers delivering infra or control changes.

Scope:
- Changes that modify RBAC v2 roles/policies, service account permissions, or default role mappings.
- Changes to audit log schema, retention, or export pipelines to SIEM.
- Introduction or modification of automated evidence collection or compliance automations.
- Any release that requires a formal sign-off or a documented exception.

Quick summary of required approvals (minimum):
- Security Reviewer (primary): validates RBAC, audit schema, SIEM mapping, risk.
- Product Owner / Feature Owner: confirms functional tradeoffs.
- Release Manager: confirms release plan and rollback.
- SRE / Infra Owner: confirms deploy/runbook and monitoring.
- Privacy/Compliance reviewer (if PII/regulated scope).

Pre-release checklist (RBAC v2):
[ ] 1) Role inventory updated: list all new/changed roles and attach the minimum set of permissions.
[ ] 2) Binding review: verify each role binding is intentional and scoped to least-privilege (principals limited to service accounts or named groups).
[ ] 3) Service account vetting: ensure any new service account has an owner, an expiry plan, and credential rotation noted.
[ ] 4) Default-role mapping: confirm no change creates a broad default role (e.g., default-allow).
[ ] 5) Delegated admin paths: explicit justification and compensating controls for any new delegate admin roles.
[ ] 6) Test matrix: automated RBAC tests included in CI (unit checks and smoke tests) and successful run attached to evidence bundle.

Audit log schema verification (required fields and sanity checks):
- Mandatory fields (each must be present and non-null for logged events):
  * timestamp (ISO8601 UTC)
  * event_id / request_id (traceable to request)
  * actor_id (user_id or service_account_id)
  * actor_type (user | service | system)
  * action (verb describing intent)
  * resource_type (model | deployment | config | secret | user)
  * resource_id (opaque id or path)
  * outcome (success | failure | denied)
  * ip_address
  * user_agent (if applicable)
  * raw_payload_hash (optional; used for integrity checks)
  * log_version (schema version, e.g. audit_v2)

Validation steps:
[ ] 1) Schema bump documented: linked PR and change-log describing field additions/semantic changes.
[ ] 2) Backwards-compatibility: consumer teams (SIEM, analytics, legal) notified and compatibility tests run.
[ ] 3) Sampling: for high-volume flows, verify sampling policy and include sampled-flag in logs.
[ ] 4) Integrity: verify hash/signature pipeline if enabled (compare raw_payload_hash across pipeline hops).

SIEM export (ingest & mapping):
- Supported export modes: encrypted syslog, cloud-pubsub export (GCP/AWS), or file-based S3 push.
- Default mapping (to be published to SIEM teams):
  * siem.time = timestamp
  * siem.event_id = event_id/request_id
  * siem.actor = actor_id
  * siem.actor_type = actor_type
  * siem.action = action
  * siem.resource = resource_type + ":" + resource_id
  * siem.outcome = outcome
  * siem.src_ip = ip_address
  * siem.user_agent = user_agent
  * siem.schema = log_version

- Export cadence & retention:
  * Near-real-time streaming for security-critical events (auth, policy changes, secrets access) -> fallback to buffered push for costed pipelines.
  * Retention policy: at least 1 year for audit-critical logs; longer retention must be justified and approved by Privacy.

- Security controls for export:
  * Always encrypt in transit and at rest (TLS + envelope encryption).
  * Strong IAM on export sink and least-privilege pushers only.
  * Re-keying/rotation plan documented for KMS keys.

Sample SIEM detection queries (example ideas for SOC):
- Detect RBAC escalation: find sequence of events where a user or group is granted admin role followed by privileged actions within 1 hour.
- Suspicious service account use: unfamiliar IPs performing management actions with a service account.
- Missing audit fields: events where log_version != expected or actor_id is null.

Evidence automation and collection (how to produce the release artifact):
- Goal: produce an immutable evidence bundle per release that contains: role diff, audit schema diff, SIEM mapping, CI test results, runbook, and automated verification outputs.
- Where artifacts land: s3://redwood-ci-evidence/<release-id>/security/ (encrypted, ACL-limited).
- Automation steps (scripted):
  1) ./tools/collect-evidence --release <id> --components rbac,audit,siem --output manifest.json
  2) Output includes checksums (sha256) and a signature placeholder for approver.
  3) CI pipeline uploads the tar.gz to the evidence S3 path and records URL in the release ticket.
  4) Security reviewer runs ./tools/verify-evidence <manifest.json> to validate checksums and required files.

- Required evidence files (minimum):
  * rbac-changes.patch (git diff or export of role changes)
  * role-binding-report.csv (current bindings snapshot)
  * audit-schema-vX.json (schema file for logs)
  * siem-mapping.md (field mapping document)
  * ci-rbac-tests.log / ci-audit-tests.log (test outputs)
  * runbook.md (deploy + rollback steps)
  * verification-report.txt (output of verify-evidence script)

Exception approval workflow (when something cannot meet the checklist):
- Exceptions are temporary deviations that must be justified, timeboxed, and include compensating controls.
- Exception request template (minimum fields):
  * exception_id: autogenerated (EXC-YYYY-NNN)
  * requested_by: name + team
  * date_requested
  * affected_components: (rbac | audit | siem | evidence)
  * description_of_gap: concise summary of what cannot be met
  * business_justification: why the exception is needed now
  * mitigation_and_compensating_controls: e.g., increased monitoring, manual approvals, IP allowlist, temporary read-only mode
  * expiration_date: must be <= 90 days unless escalated to execs
  * risk_owner: who monitors the exception and reports status
  * approval_chain: security_reviewer -> product_owner -> infra_lead (signatures/digital approval links)

- Exception decision criteria:
  * Severity assessment performed (low/medium/high)
  * Temporary controls reduce risk to acceptable level for the timeboxed window
  * A remediation plan with date committed and named owner exists

- Example mitigations that are commonly accepted for RBAC rollout exceptions:
  * Incremental rollout behind a feature-flag and monitoring for privilege elevations.
  * Manual approval gating for specific admin actions until automation is in place.

Sign-off template (fill and attach to release ticket and evidence bundle):
- Release ID: __________
- Feature / Change summary: one-line
- Scope (components): [ ] RBAC v2  [ ] Audit logs  [ ] SIEM export  [ ] Evidence automation
- Security checks completed: (checklist attached)
- Evidence bundle URL: __________

Approvals:
  Security Reviewer: __________________  date: ________  (notes: optional)
  Product Owner: _____________________  date: ________  (notes: optional)
  Release Manager: ___________________  date: ________  (notes: optional)
  SRE/Infra Owner: ___________________  date: ________  (notes: optional)
  Privacy/Compliance: _________________  date: ________  (notes: optional)

Post-release (30/90 day checks):
[ ] 30-day: verify no unexpected role escalations and SIEM detections cleared.
[ ] 90-day: confirm removal of any temporary exceptions or extension formally approved.

Common pitfalls (lessons learned):
- Not notifying SIEM/analytics consumers when schema fields change -> data loss in detections.
- Overbroad roles added to accelerate shipping -> long tail of accidental privilege exposure.
- Evidence bundles missing CI logs or checksum mismatches; automate fingerprinting earlier.

Appendix: helpful commands and links
- Verify RBAC bindings (internal tool): scripts/rbac-export.sh --env prod --format csv -> uploads to evidence bucket.
- Generate audit-schema diff: tooling/audit-schema-diff --from v1 --to v2 > audit-schema-v2.json
- Collect evidence: ./tools/collect-evidence --release <id> --output /tmp/<id>-evidence.tar.gz
- Evidence verification: ./tools/verify-evidence /tmp/<id>-evidence.tar.gz

Contact & escalation
- Primary security contact for release reviews: aisha.patel@redwood.ai
- On-call SOC (for SIEM ingestion issues): soc-oncall@redwood.ai
- Escalation path: Security Lead -> VP Engineering -> CTO (for >72h unresolved critical gaps)

Notes / open questions (working):
- Need to finalize schema versioning policy for audit logs (semver vs date-based).
- Confirm retention SLA with Legal for cross-border exports to SIEM.
- Decide on a standard long-term storage for evidence bundles (S3 vs internal archive).

End of playbook.
